final_message:
`make test` now exits 0. There were four separate problems, each masking the next:

| # | File | Problem | Symptom |
|---|------|---------|---------|
| 1 | `Makefile:4` | Recipe indented with 4 spaces, not a tab | `missing separator` |
| 2 | `scripts/run_checks.sh` | Lost executable bit (mode 644) | `Permission denied` |
| 3 | `scripts/run_checks.sh` | CRLF line endings → shebang read as `/bin/bash\r` | `No such file or directory` (exit 127) |
| 4 | `data/config.json:4` | Trailing comma after `"batch_size": 500` | `JSONDecodeError`, check failed |

All four are classic cross-machine merge damage. #3 was the interesting one — the error said the script didn't exist even though it was right there and executable; the missing file was actually the *interpreter*, since the CR became part of the shebang path.

Final state:

```
./scripts/run_checks.sh
config ok: data/config.json
all checks passed
python3 -m pytest -q tests/
...                                                                      [100%]
3 passed in 0.01s
```

Constraints respected: nothing under `tests/` was touched, no Python source changed, and no check was removed or weakened — `make test` still depends on `check`, which still runs the config validator, and the same 3 tests run. I made no git commits. I did scan every tracked file for stray CR bytes; `run_checks.sh` was the only one affected.

`SOLUTION.md` documents each problem and fix. One thing I flagged there but did not act on: problems #2 and #3 will recur on the next merge from that machine — a `.gitattributes` with `*.sh text eol=lf` would pin line endings repo-wide. I left it out as beyond the scope of getting the build green; say the word if you'd like it added.
